text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mohamed Sacirbey, Bosnia's ambassador to the U.N. in New York, supports Bosnian President Alija Izetbegovic's attempts to create a united Bosnia and says that the most important task now is to consolidate Bosnia as an integral country.

- U.S. Congress invited the deputy mayor of Mostar, Safet Orucevic, to participate in the 45th National Prayer scheduled for February 1997. The prayer will be conducted during a breakfast with U.S. President Bill Clinton and his wife.

- Robert Frowick, head of the OSCE mission in Bosnia, said on Tuesday's International Human Rights day 1997 would be a decisive year. He said the signatories of the Dayton peace agreement were no longer warring factions but established governments. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
